messages:
maria: quick sweep results from this morning — trying to pick sensible defaults for max batch tokens per device before the next runtime release. summary: built a small harness that plays back the prod seqlen histogram against each GPU type (A100/H100/A10/T4/L4), measured tokens/sec and tail latencies.

maria: baseline config we tried (dev-friendly):
```yaml
max_batch_tokens:
  L4: 1024
  T4: 2048
  A10: 4096
  A100: 16384
  H100: 32768
kernel_pref:
  L4: 'flash_attn_v1'
  others: 'flash_attn_v2'
queue_policy: 'latency_first'
```

ken: nice. two quick notes: 1) KV cache churn on chat workloads kills effective batch density — lots of short sessions means fewer multi-request batches, so tokens/sec drops vs synthetic single-stream tests. 2) we should consider a soft per-session token cap (e.g. 256) to avoid one long session stealing the batch token budget.

jia: saw a regression on L4 after we flipped to flash_attn_v2 in staging — ~12-18% throughput drop for seqlen=96 workloads. i traced it to a fallback path in the vendor kernel when sequence length % 32 != 0. switching kernel per-seqlen histogram helped.

maria: thanks. so kernel selection needs to be seqlen-aware, not just device-aware. good catch.

nick: from perf traces: A10/A100 show best throughput when we allow larger max_batch_tokens (fewer launches, better occupancy). L4/T4 prefer smaller token caps to avoid scheduling pressure. rough numbers from the run:
- L4: 1.2k tok/s, p95 48ms (max_batch_tokens=1024)
- T4: 2.6k tok/s, p95 42ms (2048)
- A10: 7.9k tok/s, p95 36ms (4096)
- A100: 28k tok/s, p95 30ms (16384)
- H100: 54k tok/s, p95 25ms (32768)

nick: also saw that memory headroom correlates with safe token budget. if memory margin < 10% we should clamp down.

sophie: proposing a simple device formula to auto-suggest defaults:
```
suggested_tokens = clamp(floor(GPU_mem_gb * 1024 / 8), min=512, max=model_max_seq*4)
```
this keeps things proportional to memory and model size. we can layer a seqlen-aware kernel table on top.

ken: +1 on memory-aware. also recommend a queue policy tweak: if queue latency > target and batch is below X% fullness, trigger a short_hold (10ms) to wait for more requests; otherwise dispatch. avoids hurting latency on bursty traffic.

maria: action items: 1) implement seqlen-aware kernel selector (jia + nick) 2) add soft per-session token cap and memory-aware auto-suggest (sophie + ken) 3) run another device sweep with canary kernel table (maria) — aim for defaults we commit to config.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/continuous-batch-tuning -> eng-runtime-canary at 2026-03-17T14:30Z :rocket:

maria: leaving a short checklist in the PR. ping me when you have the histogram-based selector ready, we can re-run with the KV churn emulator. :eyes:
